links.outcome: Documentation efficiency (WPM) and revision count, intervention vs control, non-randomized trial
links.effect: Intervention had greater WPM gains (Δ+7.2 vs Δ+2.6; group×exposure p = 0.045); revisions fell 1.36 to 1.26 per document, no significant interaction for revision count. Operational outcomes, not patient outcomes.
links.quote: Linear mixed-effects modeling confirmed a significant group × exposure interaction for documentation efficiency (p = 0.045), whereas no statistically significant interaction was observed for revision count.

links.outcome: Documentation quality via senior physician review of AI-assisted discharge letters (revision counts)
links.effect: Revision frequency decreased within intervention group (1.36 ± 0.14 to 1.26 ± 0.08 per document); no significant interaction for revision count, so standards were maintained under supervision.
links.quote: This real-world evaluation suggests that AI documentation assistance is associated with improved documentation efficiency under routine clinical conditions, while maintaining documentation standards under established supervision processes.

unlisted_practices: Inline AI suggestions using only the patient's EHR record as input, without audio, within routine workflow
Fine-tuning an LLM (QLoRA) on institutional records for documentation drafting

screen.reason: This is an empirical non-randomized controlled trial evaluating the real-world deployment of an LLM-based documentation copilot integrated into EHR workflows, assessing efficiency and revision burdens without testing an additional deployment guardrail/practice.
